messages:
anna: quick idea — autoscaler keeps launching node types that cause high fragmentation for mixed tenants. what if runtime offers a tiny "node_recommend" API that returns 2-3 concrete MIG templates + simple scores (util_range, frag_delta, warmup_s, eviction_risk) so operator can make cost tradeoffs?

devon: love the pragmatic approach. keep the API opt-in per pool. operator should be able to pass a backfill_deadline and a hard_constraint (e.g., must allow full-gpu jobs).

marc: implementation note: runtime should avoid model loads — use cached perf profiles + seq-length histograms. coalesce hints (e.g., "pair 1/4+1/4 => 1/2") would be super helpful.

jia: agree on coalesce hints. also request TTL on recommendations (e.g., ttl=10m) and a confidence band for util_range to avoid flip-flopping.

nora: eviction_risk needs to map to operator's preempt model. runtime can give ordinal risk (low/med/high) and an estimated "evictions_per_hour" so operator can compute cost.

ops-bot: infra note — rate-limit endpoint to 1/s per pool. ensure idempotent responses. create INF ticket if approved.

anna: testing plan: 1) offline sim against historical admission traces; 2) small canary pool that honors recs only when pack_opt_in=true; 3) metric watchdog to revert if pinned-job p99 latency regresses >5% in 10m.

devon: telemetry: node_recs_requested, template_selected, frag_delta_post_launch. operator should report fragment delta after launch.

marc: rollout: feature-flag per pool, default off. gradual opt-in and a rollback kill-switch.

jia: action items: anna draft RFC + example JSON responses; devon add sim job; marc add cheap coalesce knapsack; nora draft eviction_risk heuristic; ops-bot create ticket.

ops-bot: ticket INF-6200 created: "runtime node_recommend API + autoscaler integration"

anna: timeline suggestion: RFC by EOW, prototype next week, small canary in two weeks. will post RFC in channel shortly :rocket:
